clue.text: Tribal type swiftly going round hospital

indicators.note: the word for swiftly encircles the letter for hospital, so it goes round it

parts.note: apace is an old word for swiftly
H is the standard abbreviation for hospital on maps and signs

explanation.surface: A tribesman races in circles around a hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a Native American people of the Southwest is a tribesperson, so a tribal type.

clue.text: Start of rescue after one's cat got upset, one up a tree?

indicators.note: the letter from rescue follows the anagram, so comes after it
the letters of one's and cat are upset, tipped into a new order

parts.note: taken as written without the apostrophe: O, N, E, S

indicators.note: only the opening letter of rescue is used

explanation.surface: A rescuer arrives after someone's cat panicked and climbed up a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got upset' shuffles the letters of one's and cat. The tree is a family tree, where a forebear sits on a higher branch.
explanation.definitionFit: A forebear appears on a higher branch of a family tree, so is one up a tree in the genealogical sense.

clue.text: Man detained by detective in European clothing

indicators.note: the detective with his captive is placed within the word for a European

parts.note: a Turk is from Turkey, partly in Europe

indicators.note: the man is held inside the detective's word, as a suspect is detained

parts.note: tec is short for detective
Len is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man is held by a detective while wearing European garments.
explanation.walkthrough: Turkey lies partly in Europe, which lets a Turk count as European; 'detained by' and 'in' nest the pieces one inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A high-necked sweater folded over at the throat is a garment, an item of clothing.

clue.text: Ruler has disrupted hotel

indicators.note: the word has is disrupted, its letters thrown into a new order

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A ruler causes chaos at a hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of the former monarch of Iran, so a ruler.

clue.text: Way for riders free with liberal exercise taken up in historic city

indicators.note: the group of pieces is placed inside the name of the city

parts.note: Bath is a historic Roman spa city in Somerset, England
to rid is to free

indicators.note: in a down clue, taken up means the letters for exercise are read upwards, backwards

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: A path for horse riders lies free of charge in an old city, with exercise encouraged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken up' reads the exercise letters upwards, as this is a down clue. Bath is a Roman spa city in Somerset, England.
explanation.definitionFit: A track meant for horses and their riders is a way intended for those on horseback.

clue.text: A graduate on fringes of book group

indicators.note: the graduate's letters are placed around the outside of the book's letter

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: A graduate hangs around the edges of a book club.
explanation.walkthrough: BA sits on the fringes of B, giving BBA, after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: The Swedish pop act famous for Waterloo is a band, a musical group.

clue.text: Vegetable in dispute after damage

indicators.note: the dispute word follows the damage word

parts.note: to mar is to damage
a row is a dispute

explanation.surface: A vegetable is caught up in a quarrel following some harm.
explanation.definitionFit: A large green squash grown in British gardens is a vegetable.

clue.text: Smart associate managed boat

parts.note: trim means smart, neat
A is a short form of associate, as in an academic title
ran means managed, as one runs a business

explanation.surface: A smart associate was in charge of a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailing vessel with three hulls is a type of boat.

clue.text: Go round north with escort and cog in office?

indicators.note: the word for go is placed round the letter for north

parts.note: go means energy, pep
N is north
an usher escorts people to their seats

explanation.surface: Head round to the north with a chaperone and a minor clerk.
explanation.definitionFit: A low-level clerk doing routine paperwork is a small part of the office machine, a cog.

clue.text: Formerly premier or secondary haunt?

parts.note: B denotes second rank, as in B-list
a lair is a haunt, a den

explanation.surface: A question about where a former prime minister used to hang out.
explanation.walkthrough: Tony Blair was British Prime Minister 1997 to 2007.
explanation.definitionFit: A past British prime minister, Tony, who once held the premiership.

clue.text: Creature that's very fast and sharp reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the word for sharp is spoken, giving a word that sounds like it

parts.note: a sharp is a cheat or swindler, as in card sharp

explanation.surface: An animal described as very fast and clever.
explanation.walkthrough: In British non-rhotic speech, the word for a swindler sounds just like the big cat.
explanation.definitionFit: The spotted African big cat is the fastest land animal.

clue.text: Indian city seen in obscure outline

indicators.note: the city name is placed within the word for obscure

parts.note: dim means obscure, unclear
Agra is the city of the Taj Mahal

explanation.surface: An Indian city is seen as only a vague outline.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan or sketch showing the shape of something is an outline drawing.

clue.text: Take in part of programme attentively

indicators.note: only part of the words programme attentively is used, a run inside them

explanation.surface: Watch some of a broadcast carefully.
explanation.definitionFit: To consume food is to take it in.

clue.text: Noted landmark providing relief to few sadly

indicators.note: the words relief to few are badly, sadly arranged and must be reordered

explanation.surface: Relief is supplied to only a few, unfortunately.
explanation.definitionFit: The Paris iron tower is a famous monument, a well-known landmark.

clue.text: Chill and strife son's dispelled

indicators.note: the letters of strife and son's are scattered, dispelled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written without the apostrophe: S, O, N, S

explanation.surface: A family quarrel ends when the son's anger fades away.
explanation.definitionFit: Coldness of manner or weather is a chill.

clue.text: Celebrity in outing taken over part of Australia for a series of games

indicators.note: the celebrity word sits within the combined outing and territory letters
in a down clue, the outing word is placed over, above, the letters for the Australian territory

parts.note: a tour is an outing
NT is the Northern Territory of Australia
a name is a celebrity, a big name

explanation.surface: A star goes on a trip across part of Australia to play a run of matches.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'taken over' stacks the outing above the Northern Territory's letters; the celebrity then sits 'in' that combination.
explanation.definitionFit: A competition made up of many matches is a series of games.

clue.text: Keep English speciality

parts.note: a keep is a castle stronghold, a fort

explanation.surface: An English person's strong point is preserving things.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's strong point is their speciality.

clue.text: Fine sailor facing two directions to enter perhaps traditional route

parts.note: F is fine, as on a pencil
OS is an ordinary seaman

indicators.note: the two compass points go inside the word for perhaps

parts.note: say means perhaps, for example
E and W are east and west

explanation.surface: A fine sailor looks both ways before joining an old road.
explanation.walkthrough: The FOSSE WAY is a Roman road across England from Exeter to Lincoln.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient Roman road still followed today is a long-established route.

clue.text: Deliveries reported for eggs

indicators.note: reported means the word for deliveries is said aloud, giving a similar-sounding word

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries, so overs are deliveries

explanation.surface: Delivered goods turn out to be eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech, overs sounds like the plural of ovum.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural of ovum, the female reproductive cell, so eggs.

clue.text: South African city director left in a built-up area?

indicators.note: left means the director's letter has gone, departed from the city's name

parts.note: Durban is a port city in South Africa

explanation.surface: A director leaves a South African city for life in the suburbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to a town or city, so located in a built-up area.

clue.text: Garment providing a pulsating experience in confines of boutique

indicators.note: the pulsating word goes inside the boundary letters of boutique
the confines of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: a throb is a pulsation

explanation.surface: A garment in a shop's window gives a thrill.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose robe worn after bathing is an item of clothing, a garment.

clue.text: Note increased equipment with revolutionary name in homeless facility?

parts.note: so (soh) is a note in tonic sol-fa
up means increased
kit is equipment
Che Guevara was a revolutionary

explanation.surface: Raised banknote funds kit for a shelter named after a rebel.
explanation.definitionFit: A charity serving food to people without a home is a facility for the homeless.

clue.text: A French soprano in a middle of opera showing discomfort

parts.note: une is French for a

indicators.note: the soprano's letter is placed in the a and middle letter group
the central letter of opera is used

explanation.surface: A French singer appears in the middle of an opera, looking uncomfortable.
explanation.walkthrough: A plus E, the middle of opera, gives AE, and S goes inside: ASE.
explanation.definitionFit: Unease is anxiety or discomfort.

clue.text: Endlessly caustic sailor

indicators.note: endlessly means the word for caustic loses its final letter

parts.note: tart means sharp, caustic

explanation.surface: A bitter sailor who never stops being sarcastic.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack tar is an old name for a seaman, a sailor.

clue.text: Very thin figure embracing first person turning up in new version of film

indicators.note: the thin figure's word holds the first person inside it

parts.note: a rake is a very thin person

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the first-person word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: me is the first person pronoun

explanation.surface: A skinny figure embraces a lead actor appearing in a new film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses ME to EM, which RAKE embraces.
explanation.definitionFit: A fresh filming of an existing movie is a new version.

clue.text: Team shot over net

indicators.note: shot means the words over net are damaged, shot to pieces, and reordered

explanation.surface: A football team fires the ball over the net.
explanation.walkthrough: EVERTON is a Premier League football club from Liverpool.
explanation.definitionFit: A Liverpool football club is a team.

clue.text: Variety in tasty peaches

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the words tasty peaches, across the gap

explanation.surface: A kind of fruit among some delicious peaches.
explanation.definitionFit: A type is a kind, a variety.

clue.text: Monotonous stench associated with place for oil?

parts.note: hum is British slang for a bad smell
oil is stored in a drum

explanation.surface: A dull stink connected with an oil store.
explanation.definitionFit: Humdrum means dull and ordinary, so monotonous.

clue.text: Instrument actress mentioned

indicators.note: mentioned means the actress's name is spoken aloud, giving a same-sounding word

parts.note: Lena Horne was an American actress and singer

explanation.surface: An actress who is mentioned plays an instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A brass wind instrument, such as the French one, is a musical instrument.

clue.text: A piece of text right away recalled fabulous author

indicators.note: recalled means the shortened text word is called back, read in reverse
away means the letter for right is taken out

parts.note: prose is a piece of text
R is right

explanation.surface: A piece of writing, with corrections removed, brings to mind a legendary writer.
explanation.walkthrough: PROSE minus R gives POSE; 'recalled' reverses it to ESOP.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek teller of fables is an author of fables, fabulous in its literal sense.

clue.text: Special arena with approval hosting black rugby international

indicators.note: the arena and approval letters host, hold inside, the letter for black

parts.note: a ring is an arena, as in boxing
OK signals approval
B is black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A special stadium with approval hosts a black rugby player.
explanation.walkthrough: A SPRINGBOK is a player for South Africa's national rugby team.
explanation.definitionFit: A player capped for South Africa's national rugby side is a rugby international.
